specClaims.note: naive substring scan gives 101; the escape-aware scan drops 2 pattern(s) whose `\\b` is an ESCAPED BACKSLASH followed by a literal `b` (a rule matching the TEXT "\b" in source), not a word boundary.
the single corpus lookbehind is a NEGATIVE lookbehind `(?<!`; positive-lookbehind count is 0.
47 negative-lookahead ∪ 1 negative-lookbehind = 48 distinct patterns; the 3 positive-lookahead-bearing patterns all also carry a negative lookahead, so they add no new members.

opa.note: Patterns are handed to OPA as Rego RAW strings (backticks). In a Rego DOUBLE-QUOTED string `\b` is the JSON backspace escape — the double-quoted form measures U+0008, not a word boundary. `--strict-builtin-errors` is required: without it a regex COMPILE failure degrades to an undefined expression with exit 0.

failOpenProbe.label: lookahead WITHOUT --strict-builtin-errors
failOpenProbe.finding: OPA exits 0 with an empty result set. A lowerer that shells out without --strict-builtin-errors converts an inexpressible pattern into a silent NO-VIOLATION — a fail-open rule drop.

doubleQuotedStringProbe.label: regex.match("\bfoo\b", "a foo b") — DOUBLE-QUOTED form, pattern text emitted VERBATIM
doubleQuotedStringProbe.finding: false. `\b` in a Rego double-quoted string is BACKSPACE (U+0008). A lowerer that emits pattern text verbatim into a double-quoted Rego string silently breaks all 99 word-boundary-bearing patterns. Either use the raw-string form or re-escape every backslash (JSON.stringify semantics).

regoStringLiteralConstraint.finding: A Rego RAW string (backticks) has NO escape mechanism, so a regex containing a backtick cannot be carried in that form at all. This is an expressibility axis SEPARATE from RE2 syntax and it is not visible in the class partition.
regoStringLiteralConstraint.workaround: double-quoted literal with every backslash re-escaped; measured working on the affected pattern (see inexpressibleProbes[].stringForm).

expressibilityEvidenceRows.heading: GitHub auto-close keyword adjacent to an issue reference
expressibilityEvidenceRows.finding: The spec's "validateRegex rejection EXECUTED and confirmed: ReDoS vulnerability detected" REPRODUCES exactly. Beyond the spec: this pattern is nevertheless live in a SHIPPED pack corpus, so a pattern the record path's safe-regex2 gate would refuse is currently enforceable on the legacy path.
Record-authorable and RE2-inexpressible, exactly as the spec states — the cleanest single instance of the builtin gap.
The § falsification-fold N1 counts 48/47/1 and the 53-occurrence figure all reproduce exactly.

disputedRowVerdict.row: `\b` (101/226 patterns) marked unsupported by the leg's RE2 table
disputedRowVerdict.settled: FALSIFIED — `\b` IS supported by the pinned OPA (RE2/Go regexp) as an ASCII word boundary.
disputedRowVerdict.evidence: regex.match(`\bfoo\b`, "a foo b") = true; regex.match(`\bfoo\b`, "afoob") = false; the corpus pattern 61dcb058bd1df15d matches its fixture fail line and not its pass line.
disputedRowVerdict.confirmedInexpressible: lookarounds and backreferences — RE2 rejects them AT COMPILE ("invalid or unsupported Perl syntax: `(?!`", "invalid named capture: `(?<=...`", "invalid escape sequence: `\1`"), never as a silent non-match.
